{{nihongo|'''Atsuta Jingū'''|熱田神宮}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

'''Atsuta Shrine'' (Atsuta Jingu) is {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|Q80434|qid=Q80434}}{{ill|Nagoya|Q11751|qid=Q11751}}{{ill|Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Q1355625|qid=Q1355625}}{{jalink|Jingu {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in (Nagoya City)|Q30934394|Jingu}}. {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}, {{ill|Owari Province|Q514506|qid=Q514506}}{{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379|lt=Sannomiya}}. It is a shrine deeply related to {{ill|Japanese mythology|Q814158|qid=Q814158}} that enshrines the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kusanagi sword}}, and has collected {{ill|Faith|Q5410500|qid=Q5410500}} from {{ill|Ancient history|Q41493|qid=Q41493}} as "Atsuta shrine."

=== Overview ===
[[File:Minami Torii in Atsuta Jingu Shrine 2014.jpg|thumb|Minami Torii and New Year's visit crowd<br />(January 2014)]]
It is located at the southern end of {{ill|Atsuta Plateau|Q30922940|qid=Q30922940}} in the southern part of {{ill|Nagoya|Q11751|qid=Q11751}}. In ancient times, it was located on a protruding {{ill|Cape (geography)|Q185113|qid=Q185113}} in {{ill|Ise Bay|Q1368308|qid=Q1368308}}, but now that the surrounding area has been {{ill|Polder|Q106259|qid=Q106259}}, no trace of it can be seen. </ref>.It is known as a shrine that enshrines the {{ill|Kusanagi no Tsurugi|Q14944|qid=Q14944|lt=Kusanagi no Tsurugi}}, one of the {{ill|Imperial Regalia of Japan|Q327465|qid=Q327465}}. Even after it was enshrined, this sword was stolen (see "{{ill|theft of Kusanagi no Tsurugi|Q861812|qid=Q861812}}"), {{ill|Katashiro|Q11487867|qid=Q11487867}} He has suffered many hardships, including being lost during the {{ill|Battle of Dan-no-ura|Q968676|qid=Q968676}} (see "{{ill|Kusanagi no Tsurugi|Q14944|qid=Q14944}}"). Although there are various theories, the Kusanagi Shinken was founded in {{ill|Emperor Keikō|Q329723|qid=Q329723}} in 1943. * {{ill|Takeinadane|Q11486691|qid=Q11486691}}Regarding Atsuta Omikami, the main deity enshrined, Atsuta Shrine says, ``Amaterasu Omikami, who brings forth the Kusanagi Sword, one of the three sacred treasures, as a divine spirit.''<ref name="Jingu 7">Atsuta Jingu: Page 7</ref> In other words, it refers to Amaterasu Omikami as the ``true identity'' of the Kusanagi Sword; in other words, the Kusanagi Sword itself is ``Atsuta Omikami'' as the ``substance'' of Amaterasu Omikami. {{ill|Pre-war|Q7239276|qid=Q7239276|lt=Before the war}}, the main enshrined deity was "Kusanagi Omikken-jin" ("Atsuta Jingu abbreviation" (1877 (Meiji 10))) <ref name="Jingu Shrine Historical Materials Auspicious Origin History 339">"Atsuta Jingu Historical Materials Auspicious Origin Edition": page 339</ref>, "Amatsumi Shirushi Chrysalis Ohomitsurugi" ("Atsuta Jingu Abbreviation" (1939)) <ref name="abbreviation 1">``Atsuta Jingu abbreviation'': 1 page</ref>, but no distinction was made between the true identity and the spirit age in terms of expression. However, the idea that the Kusanagi sword is Amaterasu Omikami is an old one that already appears in the Atsuta Myojin Koshiki (late Heian period). /rt></ruby>'''Amaterasu Omikami's true form'', Konno Omiya Gongen Koreya (If you listen to the classic scriptures, Murakumo is the true identity of Amaterasu Omiya, the present Omiya Gongen.)'' (Atsuta Myojin Lectures <ref name="Jingu Historical Materials 22">"Atsuta Jingu Historical Materials: 22 pages")|group="Note"}}. However, in the older ``{{ill|Owari no Kuni Fudoki|Q135598023|qid=Q135598023}},'' there is an image of Japan Takeru when he handed over the Kusanagi sword to Miyazaki Hime. {{#tag:ref | Indeed, this sword has the <ruby><rb>spirit</rb><rt> of God</rt></ruby>. Mikage</rt></ruby> and <ruby><rb><br></rb><rt>Set</rt></ruby>, and <ruby><rb>Cause</rb><rt></rt></ruby> set up <ruby><rb>company</rb><rt>Yashiro</rt></ruby>, <ruby><r The name is derived from <ruby><rb>y</rb><rt> from b>鄕</rb><rt>sato</rt></ruby> (Atsuta-go).'' name="Fudōki 246">``Complete Japanese Classical Works ``Fudōki'' Part 2'': page 246</ref>)|group="Note"}}, it is said that in the Nara period there was a view that Japan Takeru was the true identity of the Kusanagi Shinken.<ref name="Shin-Nagoya City History 1_524">"New Nagoya City History Volume 1": 524 pages</ref> Since the Heian period, it has been a common belief that the true identity of the Kusanagi sword is Amaterasu Omikami, the deity enshrined at the Imperial Shrine (Inner Shrine) in Ise. name="Shin-Nagoya City History 2_334">"New Nagoya City History Volume 2": page 334 It has even been said that they are the two supporting pillars. ``Nihon Ni''''<ruby><rb>'''并''''</rb><rt>Hashira</rt></ruby>'''The God'' The name of Japan's divine kingdom is for the benefit of sentient beings, the place of the Southern Enfudai, the name of Shinmei is given, and the birth of the Buddha is the most important thing. name="Jingu Historical Materials 28">Atsuta Jingu Historical Materials: 28 pages</ref>)|group="Note"}}.The shrine enshrines Amaterasu Omikami, Sujin no Mikoto, Nihon Takeru, Miyasa Hime no Mikoto, Kenine Tane no Mikoto, and other gods related to Kusanagi Tsurugi. When Sujinson defeated {{ill|Yamata no Orochi|azb|یاماتا نو اوروچی|bcl|Yamata no Orochi|ca|Yamata-no-Orochi|de|Yamatanoorochi|es|Yamata-no-Orochi|fa|یاماتا نو اوروچی|fr|Yamata-no-Orochi|hu|Jamata no Orocsi|id|Yamata-no-Orochi|it|Yamata no Orochi|ja|ヤマタノオロチ|ko|야마타노오로치|lb|Yamata no Orochi|lt|Jamata no Oroči|no|Hachimata|pl|Yamata no Orochi|pt|Yamata no Orochi|ru|Ямата-но ороти|simple|Yamata-no-Orochi|sq|Jamata no Oroçi|sr|Јамата но Ороћи|sv|Yamata no Orochi|ta|யமத்தா நோ ஒரொச்சி|th|ยามาตะ โนะ โอโรจิ|tr|Yamata no Orochi|uk|Ямата-но ороті|vi|Yamata no Orochi|zh|八岐大蛇|qid=Q1054437}}, he found the Kusanagi sword in the tail of Yamata no Orochi and presented it to Amaterasu Omikami. Amaterasu Omikami gave the Kusanagi sword to {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Q1056017|qid=Q1056017|lt=Ninigi no Mikoto}} (Ninigi no Mikoto) at the time of {{ill|Tenson kōrin|Q1084733|qid=Q1084733}}. After taking the Kusanagi sword and playing an active role in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ezo conquest}}, Takeru of Japan entrusted it to his wife, Miyazaki Hime-no-Mikoto. Miyazakihime no Mikoto established the land of Atsuta as {{ill|Divination|af|Wiggelary|ami|Pi’arawan to sorit: Mi’edaw|ar|كهانة|az|Divinasiya|be_x_old|Варажба|bg|Предсказание|bn|ভবিষ্যদ্‌বাণী|ca|Endevinació|co|Divinazione|cs|Věštba|cy|Darogan|da|Divination|de|Divination (Religionswissenschaft)|eo|Divenado|es|Adivinación|et|Ennustamine|eu|Aurresan|fa|طالع‌بینی|fi|Divinaatio|fr|Divination|gl|Adiviñación|he|ניחוש|hi|दैववाणी|hr|Proricanje|hu|Jóslás|ia|Divination|id|Ramalan|it|Divinazione|ja|占い|ka|მკითხაობა|kbp|Tɩʋ pazɩyʋ|kk|Көріпкелдік|ko|점복|ky|Төлгө|mg|Vinany (fanao)|mk|Претскажување|ms|Penilikan|nia|Fama'ele'ö|nl|Wichelarij|nn|Klarsyn|oc|Divinacion|pl|Wróżenie|pt|Adivinhação|qu|Watuq|ru|Предсказание|sah|Хаартынан билгэлээһин|scn|Arriminavintura|sh|Proricanje|simple|Divination|sk|Veštenie|sr|Прорицање|sv|Spådomskonst|tr|Divinasyon|tt|Тәкъдир|uk|Пророкування|ur|کہانت|vi|Bói toán|zh|占卜|zh_classical|筮|zh_yue|占卜|qid=Q1043197|lt=Bokusei}} and enshrined the Kusanagi sword. Kenine Tane-no-Mikoto was the older brother of Miyasa Hime-no-Mikoto, and served as an adjutant general in Japan Takeru's conquest of Ezo.As the ``Engishiki'' Volume 3 God Gizo (temporary festival) and Volume 9 Shinto Name Book say ``Atsuta Shrine Ichiza'' <ref name="Engishiki 194">"Engishiki 1": page 94</ref><ref name="Engishiki 2123">"Engishiki 2nd": page 123</ref>, it is highly likely that only the sacred sword was enshrined until ancient times.<ref name="Shin-Nagoya City History 1_522">"New Nagoya City History Volume 1": 522 pages</ref>. According to legend, the sacred sword was transferred from the capital in 686 (the first year of Shucho), but in reality, probably after the Middle Ages when the influence of the syncretism of Shinto and Buddhism became evident, the sacred sword was enshrined in the Doyoden and the five gods were enshrined in the Seiden.{{# tag:ref|``At the time of Emperor Tenmu's return from Miyako (the capital), he rebuilt the Doyo Palace, put the sacred sword in a stone chest, and enshrined it in Dochu.'' (Bishu Jingu Hiden) <ref name="Jingu Historical Materials, Origin and History Sequel 3">'Atsuta Shrine Historical Materials, Engiance and History Sequel (1)': 3 pages</ref>)|group="Note"}}. After Doyoden was abolished in 1893 (Meiji 26), the main shrine was enshrined with the five deities of the main deity, the Kusanagi sword and the Aiden deity. name="Shin-Nagoya City History 1_522-523">"New Nagoya City History Volume 1": pages 522-523</ref>.

=== Founding and founding ===
The Kusanagi divine sword is said to have been born from the tail of Sosanagi when he defeated {{ill|Yamata no Orochi|azb|یاماتا نو اوروچی|bcl|Yamata no Orochi|ca|Yamata-no-Orochi|de|Yamatanoorochi|es|Yamata-no-Orochi|fa|یاماتا نو اوروچی|fr|Yamata-no-Orochi|hu|Jamata no Orocsi|id|Yamata-no-Orochi|it|Yamata no Orochi|ja|ヤマタノオロチ|ko|야마타노오로치|lb|Yamata no Orochi|lt|Jamata no Oroči|no|Hachimata|pl|Yamata no Orochi|pt|Yamata no Orochi|ru|Ямата-но ороти|simple|Yamata-no-Orochi|sq|Jamata no Oroçi|sr|Јамата но Ороћи|sv|Yamata no Orochi|ta|யமத்தா நோ ஒரொச்சி|th|ยามาตะ โนะ โอโรจิ|tr|Yamata no Orochi|uk|Ямата-но ороті|vi|Yamata no Orochi|zh|八岐大蛇|qid=Q1054437}}. b>Cut the <ruby><rb>snake</rb><rt>orochi</rt></ruby> on the <ruby><rb>tail</rb><rt>o</rt></ruby>. As it grows, the <ruby><rb>sword</rb><rt> of the <ruby><rb>sword</rt></ruby> will not come</rt></ruby>, so if you pry its tail open, there will be a sword inside. ``It's Yuru<ruby><rb>Kusanagi</rb><rt>Kusanagi no</rt></ruby><ruby><rb>Tsurugi</rt></ruby>'' (Nihon Shoki (Vol. 1 Jindai 8th section) <ref. name="Nihon Shoki 1 67">"Kana Nihon Shoki Volume 1": page 67</ref>)|group="Note"}}. It appears in "Kojiki" (Volume 1) as "Tsumugari no Tachi" (a beautiful name for a sharp long sword).<ref name="Kojiki 29">"Front Notes Konbun Kojiki": page 29</ref>, "Nihonshoki" (Volume 1, Jindai, 8th section, 1st book) states that the original name is "'''Ama no Murakumo no Tsurugi'"<ref name="Nihonshoki 1 67">"Kana Nihonshoki Volume 1": page 67</ref>. This book is said to mainly quote ``Nihonshoki'' from many sources including ``Kojiki'' and ``Owari Province Fudoki,'' and the book itself is said to have little originality. On the other hand, it is said that there are few distortions of the original text, and faithful quotations are made, and even though it was written in the Kamakura period, the content itself is said to have documentary value as being from the Heian period or earlier. Above all, this book is unique in that it describes how Kenine Tane-no-Mikoto guided him to the mansion in Hikami-mura, where he met Miyazuhime and spent their days together, and how he stopped by Hikami-mura again on his way back from his eastern expedition. The statement that Atsuta was chosen as the place of worship by fortune-telling indicates that the sacred treasure of Amaterasu Omikami was brought to Atsuta via the imperial family's Ise Shrine, and is an important point for Atsuta Shrine to flaunt its noble legitimacy.However, as {{ill|Kyūya Osaki|Q11465166|qid=Q11465166}} points out, "Owari Province Atsuta Daijingu Enki" explains why the place chosen for the shrine (Atsuta) came to be called Atsuta. Although the location of the shrine was determined, there is no record of when the shrine was founded and the Kusanagi Shinken was transferred there, or whether the shrine itself was founded or relocated.<ref name="Historical Materials Review 36">"Atsuta Shrine Historical Materials Review": 36 pages</ref>. Furthermore, the place where Hime protected and worshiped the Kusanagi sword after her death, that is, the place where it was transferred, is actually vaguely described (it does not say that it was Atsuta or Hikami-mura) <ref name="Historical Reference 36"/>. The ambiguity of ``Owari Province Atsuta Daijingu Enki'' was supplemented by various enki and history books that appeared in later years.

=== Outline ===
The {{ill|Gūji|Q11453500|qid=Q11453500|lt=grand chief priest}} position was held by the {{ill|Owari clan|Q11465311|qid=Q11465311}}, a descendant of Kunizo Owari, for generations, but in the late {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}} The position was given to {{ill|Fujiwara no Suenori|Q11623142|qid=Q11623142}} of {{ill|Fujiwara Nan-ke|Q2975332|qid=Q2975332}}, who was {{ill|grandson|Q11430412|qid=Q11430412}} of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Owara member position}}. Since then, the descendants of the {{ill|Fujiwara Nan-ke|Q2975332|qid=Q2975332}}{{ill|Fujiwara clan|Q641628|qid=Q641628}} and {{Ruby|[[:Category:Chiaki family|Chiaki]]|senshu}} families have continued to serve as Daiguji, and the Owari clan has continued to serve as Gonguji. Furthermore, this daughter of Suenori is the mother of {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800|qid=Q242800}} ({{ill|Yura Gozen|Q11577620|qid=Q11577620}}). In addition, Suenori's adopted daughter (real grandchild) was married to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yoshiyasu Ashikaga}} (ancestor of {{ill|Ashikaga clan|Q725370|qid=Q725370}}), and this lineage has been passed down to the Ashikaga clan as well. Furthermore, Kihan's younger sister is the mother of {{ill|Nikaidō Yukimasa|Q11371903|qid=Q11371903}}, and has a close relationship with {{ill|Nikaidō clan|Q2000952|qid=Q2000952}}.

``{{ill|Kaidōki|Q11559314|qid=Q11559314}}'' says, ``If you pass the palace of Atsuta no Miya,'' and ``{{ill|Tōkan Kikō|Q11528660|qid=Q11528660|lt=Tokan Kiko}}'' says, ``You will arrive at Atsuta no Miya, the land of Owari.'' Also in the same book,
{{Quotation|Someone said, ``This shrine is Susano no Mikoto, and the shrine was first built in the country of Izumo.Yakumo stands [(*') Yakumo Tatsu Izumo Yaegaki Build a Yaegaki in Tsumago (*') (Kojiki)] This is also the origin of the Yamato word. Later, during the reign of Emperor Keiko, this stone was left behind. ” he said. He also says, ``The main body of this shrine is the sacred sword that is dedicated to Kusanagi.When Keiyuki's son, Nihon Takeru, returns home after giving up his life, he becomes a swan and departs, and his sword rests in Atsuta.''
|Kokumin Tosho Co., Ltd.|Tokyo Travelogue (School Note: Nippon Bungaku University 3)}}

{{ill|Zuikei Shūhō|Q11573918|qid=Q11573918}}'s Gaun Diary {{ill|1465|Q6556|qid=Q6556}} ({{ill|Kanshō|Q1143928|qid=Q1143928}}6) June 18th article states, ``'''Japan's so-called three great chief priests'''' , Itsukushima, Atsuta, and Fujino Sanshoya,'' and Atsuta Daiguji is counted as one of Japan's three great chief priests, along with {{ill|Itsukushima kannushi family|Q11410131|qid=Q11410131}} and {{ill|Fuji clan|Q11456091|qid=Q11456091}}<ref>{{Cite book|Japanese book|author={{ill|Historiographical Institute|Q11524667|qid=Q11524667}}|title=Dainippon Ancient Records Gaun Nichirenroku Extract|date=1961|publisher=Iwanami Shoten|isbn=|pages=161}}</ref>.{{ill|Sengoku period|Q204023|qid=Q204023|lt=In the Sengoku period}}, the Chiaki family served the Oda family as military commanders, and {{ill|Kimitsu Chiaki|Q95512679|qid=Q95512679}} was {{ill|Oda Nobuhide|Q1153962|qid=Q1153962}}, Suimitsu's child {{ill|Senshū Suetada|Q11405793|qid=Q11405793|lt=Suitada}} serves {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|Q171411|qid=Q171411}}. Before the {{ill|Battle of Okehazama|Q349422|qid=Q349422}}, Nobunaga prayed for victory at Atsuta Shrine and won a spectacular victory, but Suetada died in the battle, and Nobunaga inherited the post of Grand Shrine and his estate to Suetada's son {{ill|Senshū Suenobu|Q116937389|qid=Q116937389|lt=Suenobu}}, who was still in the womb.

Also, it is described as ``Atsuta Daijingu'' in ``{{ill|Tōkaidō meisho zue|Q48746095|qid=Q48746095}}''.In June of {{ill|Keiō|Q776775|qid=Q776775}} 4th year ({{ill|1868|Q7717|qid=Q7717}}), it was declared {{ill|List of Jingū|Q120680118|qid=Q120680118}} and the name was changed from Atsuta Shrine to Atsuta Jingu. {{ill|1871|Q7746|qid=Q7746}}{{ill|July 1|Q2700|qid=Q2700}} (Meiji 4th year {{jalink|May 14th With the establishment of the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} on (old calendar)|Q839544|May 14th}}, Atsuta Shrine was ranked as {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Kanpei Taisha}}. There was an argument that Atsuta Jingu ``enshrines one of the three sacred treasures, so it should be on the same level as {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|qid=Q687168}}'', and in July of the same year, Grand Priest Chiaki Kifuku petitioned the government to give it the same treatment as Ise Jingu, but this petition was rejected. Tadayuki Tsunoda, who subsequently became Daiguji, continued to make similar petitions, and by {{ill|1889|Q7831|qid=Q7831}} (Meiji 22), the divine seal and the establishment of a Gonguji, similar to those at Ise Grand Shrine, were approved.Until then, Atsuta Shrine had been built in Owari-zukuri, an architectural style unique to the Owari region, but in 1889 (Meiji 22), plans were made to construct the shrine building in the same Shinmei-zukuri style as Ise Jingu. Furthermore, as a result of Atsuta Jingu's approach to the government, in September 1890|Q7832}, a proposal was submitted to the Cabinet to remove it from the status of a shrine and make it the same status as Ise Jingu (at the draft stage, the proposal included renaming Atsuta Jingu to ``Owari Jingu'', but this was removed). However, this imperial edict was rejected, and the status of Atsuta Jingu as a shrine remained as before. It is said that the reason behind this was opposition from Ise Grand Shrine. Construction of the shrine building in Shinmei-zukuri style continued and was completed in {{ill|1893|Q7840|qid=Q7840}} (Meiji 26). However, this shrine building, along with other buildings, was attacked by air raids during {{ill|Pacific War|Q184425|qid=Q184425}}.

First of all, in the air raid on March 12th, {{ill|1945|Q5240|qid=Q5240}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}}20), the Chinkomon Gate, Togakusho, Kagura Hall, Shinto Talisman Awarding Office, Imperial Embassy, Saikan, Imperial Palace, etc. were destroyed by fire. |publisher=Tokyo Shoseki |year=2016-09-29 |page=610 |isbn=978-4-487-74409-1}}</ref>. It was then burnt down in the {{ill|Bombing of Atsuta|Q11569122|qid=Q11569122}} on June 9 of the same year.Also, just before the end of the war, a temporary relocation to {{ill|Minashi Shrine|abstract|Q704865|fr|Minashi-jinja|ja|飛騨一宮水無神社|zh|飛驒一宮水無神社|qid=Q704865}} was planned to protect the sacred Kusanagi sword, but this was temporarily canceled due to the end of the war on {{ill|August 15|Q2774|qid=Q2774}} of the same year. *1364 (Teiji 3rd year, Shohei 19th year) - '''Seiji Meishin'' [Seijen Meishin] (``Owari Domestic Shinto Name Book'' Teiji version <ref name="Shinja Guroku 1808"/>)

=== Chronology ===
〈〉 indicates related matters.
*(Tradition) Year of Emperor Koan - Hiwarimiko Shrine is founded <ref name="Jingu 20">'Atsuta Jingu': page 20</ref>.
*(Tradition) Before the reign of Emperor Keiko - Magowakamiko Shrine is built (``Atsuta Daijingu Sonmyo Matsuri Shinki'' <ref name="Jingu Historical Materials Auspicious History 320">``Atsuta Shrine Historical Materials Auspicious History Edition'': page 320</ref>).
*(Tradition) Emperor Keiko's 43rd year - {{ill|Yamato Takeru|Q461258|qid=Q461258|lt=Nihon Takeru}} passed away in Nobono. The Kusanagi sword is enshrined.
*(Tradition) During the reign of Emperor Keiko - Ichinogozen Shrine is established (``Atsuta Daijingu Enshrined Deity Shintai Honki'' <ref name="Jingu Historical Materials Engiyoshi 139">``Atsuta Jingu Historical Materials Engiyoshi 139'': page 139</ref>).
*(Tradition) 4th year of Emperor Chuai - Miyakami Hime-no-Mikoto dies, and a shrine (Hikami Aneko Shrine) is built on the grounds of Motomiya ("Owari Province Hikami Shrine Start Seiden Honki" <ref name="Jingu Historical Materials Engi Yoshiro 405" />).

*{{ill|708|Q23511|qid=Q23511}} ({{ill|Wadō (era)|Q1373026|qid=Q1373026}} 1st year) September 9 - Hakkengu Shrine is founded (``Atsuta Jingu Shintai Biography'' <ref name="Jingu Historical Materials Engi History 157">``Atsuta Jingu Historical Materials Engi History Edition'': page 157</ref>).**There is also a theory that it was founded in 686 (the first year of Shucho) (``Atsuta Jingu Seienki'' <ref name="Jingu Historical Materials Engi History 131">``Atsuta Jingu Historical Materials Engi History Edition'': page 131</ref>).

*{{ill|907|Q24163|qid=Q24163}} ({{ill|Engi (era)|Q1374325|qid=Q1374325}}7 years) - Added to {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}{{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}.
*{{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}} ({{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=extension}}5 years) December 26 - <Completion of "{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}"
*{{ill|967|Q23699|qid=Q23699}} ({{ill|Kōhō|Q1327182|qid=Q1327182}}4th year) July 9th - ``Engishiki'' implemented.
*1000 (Choho 2) - Minami-Shingu Shrine is founded (``Atsuta Daijingu Shintai Hessho'' <ref name="Jingu Historical Materials Engi Yoshio Sequel 179">``Atsuta Jingu Historical Materials Engi Yoshio Sequel (Part 1)'': page 179</ref>).**There is also a theory that it was founded in 1023 ({{ill|Jian (era)|Q1150852|qid=Q1150852|lt=Security}}3).
*1093 (Kanji 7) - ``I hereby decree that the Lords of Owari will rise from the shrine on the national fire'' (Hyakurensho <ref name="Kokushi Taikei 14_56">Kokushi Taikei Vol. 14: page 56</ref>).
**Indicates that a strange incident occurred at Hikami Aneko Shrine in which a fallen tree stood up, and a countermeasures meeting was held at the Imperial Court.
*1160 (Heiji 2) New Year - {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshitomo|Q532301|qid=Q532301}}, who was defeated in the Heiji Rebellion, stops at Hikami Aneko Shrine and prays for the prosperity of the Genji clan and offers a sword ("Changshu Fushi" <ref name="Changshu Fushiichi 88">"Changshu Fushiichi": page 88</ref>).
*{{ill|1190|Q19736|qid=Q19736}} ({{ill|Kenkyū|Q1193933|qid=Q1193933}} first year) - {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800|qid=Q242800}} dedicated the sword (jokurokujosha visit offering).
*{{ill|1194|Q19743|qid=Q19743}} (Kenkyu 5th year) and {{ill|1195|Q19745|qid=Q19745}} (Kenkyu 6th year) - Minamoto no Yoritomo dedicated the sword in two parts. Respectively, the envoy {{ill|Ōe no Hiromoto|Q384829|qid=Q384829}} presented the envoy and returned to Tokyo.
*{{ill|1335|Q6011|qid=Q6011}} ({{ill|Kenmu|Q1193970|qid=Q1193970|lt=Kenmu}}2) - {{ill|Ashikaga Takauji|Q297107|qid=Q297107}} dedicated a sword (visited on a pilgrimage to Kyoto).*{{ill|1377|Q6289|qid=Q6289}} ({{ill|Eiwa|Q1145780|qid=Q1145780|lt=Eiwa}}3 years) - Dedicated "{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}" (Atsuta version).
*{{ill|1382|Q6335|qid=Q6335}} ({{ill|Eitoku|Q1145805|qid=Q1145805}}3) - Fire at Hikami Aneko Shrine. As a result, the place name was changed from Hodaka Higami to Otaka Hikami.
*July 9, 1419 (June 17, 2016) - On the occasion of the transfer of the Watariden, {{ill|Ashikaga Yoshimochi|Q466287|qid=Q466287}} dedicates a sword, a mirror, the Lotus Sutra, etc. (Atsuta Shrine Chronicles <ref name="Jingu Historical Materials Construction Sengu Volume 1": page 60</ref>).
*February 6, 1423 (December 25, 29th year of Oei) - Yoshimochi Ashikaga dedicates a sacred horse to the construction and transfer of Ohukuda Shrine, which was burnt down in 1415 (22nd year of Oei). Volume 1: pages 61-62</ref>).
*January 5, 1445 (November 27, 1st year of Bun'an) - The Ashikaga Shogun family dedicates a sword and a horse to the Gendayu Shrine Main Hall ("Atsuta Shrine Chronicles" <ref name="Jingu Shrine Historical Materials Construction and Sengu Volume 1": page 66</ref>).*July 9, 1451 (June 11, 1451) - The Ashikaga shogun family dedicated a sword and a horse to the construction of Omiya Toyoden ("Atsuta Shrine Chronicles" <ref name="Jingu Shrine Historical Materials Construction Sengu Volume 1": page 67</ref>).
*{{ill|1560|Q6613|qid=Q6613}} ({{ill|Eiroku|Q1143341|qid=Q1143341}}3rd year) - {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|Q171411|qid=Q171411}} dedicated {{ill|tsuijibei|Q11603471|qid=Q11603471}} (Nobunaga wall).
*{{ill|Number of the beast|Q666|qid=Q666}} ({{ill|Genki (era)|Q1145064|qid=Q1145064}}2nd year) - Oda Nobunaga repairs the shrine building and builds a new Kaizomon (Sea Gate)<ref name="atsutarekishi">[https://www.city.nagoya.jp/kankobunkakoryu/page/0000054494.html Historic sights that should be maintained and improved in Nagoya City 2]</ref>.
*March 31, 1572 (February 18, 3rd year of Genki) - {{ill|Sakuma Nobumori|Q3275789|qid=Q3275789}}, rebuilds Toyoden ("Gozoei Chronki" <ref name="Jingu Historical Materials Construction and Sengu 78">"Atsuta Jingu Historical Materials Construction and Sengu Edition Volume 1": page 78</ref>).
*June 2, 1590 (May 1, Tensho 18) - {{ill|Ōmandokoro|Q5353737|qid=Q5353737}} visits the shrine and dedicates 123 kanmon as the firstfruits ("Atsuta Shrine Chronicles" <ref name="Jingu Historical Materials Zoei Sengu 71">"Atsuta Jingu Historical Materials Zoei Sengu Edition Vol. 1": page 71</ref>).*1591 (Tensho 19) - {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Q187550|qid=Q187550}} repairs the shrine building<ref name="atsutarekishi"/>.
*1593 (Bunroku 2) - Toyotomi Hideyoshi became the main owner, and the roof of the Seiden was repaired ("Gozoei Chronki" <ref name="Jingu Historical Materials Zokei Sengu 8/78"/>).
*July 22, 1598 (June 19, 1598) - Emperor Toyotomi Hideyoshi (Atsutamiya Chronicles <ref name="Jingu Historical Materials Construction Sengu 71"/>).
*1599 (Auspicious day of August 4th year of Keicho era) - {{ill|Asano Nagamasa|Q1067546|qid=Q1067546}}, rebuilds the main hall of Hakkengu Shrine ("Gozoei Chronki" <ref name="Jingu Historical Materials Construction and Sengu Volume 1": pages 78-79</ref>).
*1600 (Keicho 5) - {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|qid=Q171977}} repairs the shrine, and {{ill|Katō Kiyomasa|Q1069843|qid=Q1069843}} constructs the Chinnomon Gate.<ref name="atsutarekishi"/>
*1601 (Auspicious day of June 6th year of Keicho era) - Hakkengu Shrine Roofing by Asano Nagamasa ("Atsuta Shrine Chronicles" <ref name="Jingu Historical Materials Construction Sengu 72">"Atsuta Jingu Historical Materials Construction Sengu Volume 1": page 72</ref>).
*1603 (July 8th year of Keicho) - Tokugawa Ieyasu restores Hakkengu Shrine ("Gozoei Chronki" <ref name="Jingu Historical Materials Construction and Sengu Volume 1">"Atsuta Jingu Historical Materials Construction and Sengu Volume 1": page 79</ref>).*1606 (Auspicious day of September 11th year of Keicho era) - {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyori|Q313641|qid=Q313641}} orders {{ill|Katagiri Katsumoto|Q1882775|qid=Q1882775}} to rebuild the 9-ringed treasure pagoda of Jingu-ji Temple ("Gozoei Chronki" <ref name="Jingu Historical Materials Construction Sengu 179"/>).
*August 27, 1613 (July 12, Keicho 18) - {{ill|Tokugawa Hidetada|Q314464|qid=Q314464}} (Atsutamiya Chronicles <ref name="Jingu Historical Materials Construction Sengu 1st 72"/>).
*1618 (Auspicious day of March 4th year of Genna) - {{ill|Hachisuka Iemasa|Q1073557|qid=Q1073557}}, constructs Takaza Yumiko Shrine ("Gozoei Chronki" <ref name="Jingu Historical Materials Construction Sengu 79"/>).
*June 12, 1619 (May 1, 1619) - {{ill|Tokugawa Yoshinao|Q1136186|qid=Q1136186}}, the main building Tsukiji was repaired (Atsuta Shrine Chronicles <ref name="Jingu Historical Materials Construction and Sengu Volume 1">Page 73</ref>).
*January 29, 1623 (December 29, 1623) - Tokugawa Yoshinao repairs Kaizomon, Sanzo, Gakusho, Togaki, Shunshumon, and Gokusho (Atsutamiya Chronicles <ref name="Jingu Historical Materials Construction Sengu 173"/>).
*December 21, 1629 (November 7, Kanei 6) - {{ill|Tokugawa Iemitsu|Q314481|qid=Q314481}} dedicates 100 koku of rice as a first-fruits offering (Atsutamiya Chronicles <ref name="Jingu Historical Materials Construction Sengu 73"/>).*{{ill|1839|Q7616|qid=Q7616}} ({{ill|Tenpō|Q1369045|qid=Q1369045}}10) January 19th - An attempt by a demon priest to steal the sacred object of Hakkengu Shrine.
*{{ill|1868|Q7717|qid=Q7717}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} first year)

*{{ill|1893|Q7840|qid=Q7840}} (Meiji 26) - Renovated from {{ill|Owari-zukuri|Q11465322|qid=Q11465322}} to Shinmei-zukuri.
*{{ill|1914|Q2083|qid=Q2083}} (Taisho 3) April 7: "Japanese Takeru 1800th Anniversary Festival" is held.
*August 1933 - The {{ill|Nagoya Castle|Q648629|qid=Q648629|lt=Nagoya Imperial Villa}} Karikensho building, which was given to Atsuta Shrine by the Imperial Household Agency on the occasion of the Showa Tairei ceremony, is moved to Hikami Aneko Shrine and becomes a shrine of worship.
*{{ill|1945|Q5240|qid=Q5240}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}}20)
**This year, the city suffered damage from several air raids.**May 17th - Various shrine buildings and the {{ill|National Treasure (Japan)|Q1139795|qid=Q1139795}} Sea Gate <ref>[http://network2010.org/article/117 Network2010 (Nagoya/Atsuta Shrine Nobunaga Wall and Sea Gate in the Taisho period)]</ref> built by Oda Nobunaga were destroyed by fire.
**June 9 - Damaged by {{ill|Bombing of Atsuta|Q11569122|qid=Q11569122}}.
**July 29 - The national treasure Jinkomon Gate built by Kiyomasa Kato burns down.
**August 21st - The object of worship was moved to {{ill|Minashi Shrine|abstract|Q704865|fr|Minashi-jinja|ja|飛騨一宮水無神社|zh|飛驒一宮水無神社|qid=Q704865}}.
**September 19th - The object of worship was moved to Atsuta Shrine.
**December 15th - <{{ill|Shinto Directive|Q3029647|qid=Q3029647}}>

*March 2, 1947 - The main shrine of Takaza Yumiko Shrine is rebuilt and the Kanza Festival is held.
*{{ill|1955|Q18577|qid=Q18577}} (Showa 30) October - Reconstruction.
*{{ill|1963|Q2755|qid=Q2755}} (1963) - Rebuilt Takaza Yumiko Shrine.*June 28, 1970 - Enshrining ceremony of Kotoseyama Shrine is held <ref name="Jingu 32">"Atsuta Jingu": page 32</ref>.
*{{ill|2007|Q2024|qid=Q2024}} ({{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}}19) October 22nd - Due to the renovation of the main shrine, the ``Kariden Transfer Ceremony'' will be held to move the deity to the temporary shrine.
*{{ill|2009|Q1996|qid=Q1996}} (Heisei 21) October 10th - The ``Honden Transfer Festival'' is held to move the deity to the main shrine.
*{{ill|2013|Q1998|qid=Q1998}} (Heisei 213) May 8th - "The 1900th Anniversary Festival" will be held.
*{{ill|2021|Q49628|qid=Q49628}} (Reiwa 4) - As part of the celebratory project commemorating the enthronement of the Emperor, Kusanagi Square (renovated) was opened on July 1st, and {{ill|Treasure Trove of Swords Kusanagi-kan|Q110259947|qid=Q110259947}} (newly built) was opened on October 3rd.

* Main shrine - The main shrine, which is the center of the main shrine, was originally built in {{ill|1893|Q7840|qid=Q7840}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}26), and has been renovated several times to date. The building area is 60.7 square meters, the architectural style is Shinmei-zukuri, the roof is covered with copper plates, and it is crowned with {{ill|chigi and katsuogi|Q87220234|qid=Q87220234|lt=Chigi/Katsuogi}}. There are roundabouts and railings on all sides, and a wooden staircase on the south facade. The dugout pillars are set with stone.

* Nobunaga Wall - {{ill|Eiroku|Q1143341|qid=Q1143341}}3rd year ({{ill|1560|Q6613|qid=Q6613}}) {{ill|May 19 (Lunisolar)|Q839577|qid=Q839577|lt=May 19th}}, {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|Q171411|qid=Q171411}} and his troops stopped by on their way to {{ill|Battle of Okehazama|Q349422|qid=Q349422}} and prayed for victory. After the battle, part of the wall that Nobunaga built as a thank you for his victory still exists, and is considered one of Japan's three greatest earthen walls.

* Senshukaku - A Sukiya-style tea room completed on June 25, {{ill|1950|Q18597|qid=Q18597}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}}25). Renovated in July {{ill|1989|Q2425|qid=Q2425}} ({{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}} first year).
* Guest hall* {{ill|Matabei|Q122382294|qid=Q122382294}} (National {{ill|Registered Tangible Cultural Property of Japan|Q11579194|qid=Q11579194}}) - Former Sakagami family residence. {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}} built in the middle of the {{ill|Hida Province|Q1056535|qid=Q1056535|lt=Hida}} region, {{ill|1936|Q18649|qid=Q18649}} (1937), moved to {{ill|Shōwa-ku|Q1155273|qid=Q1155273}}, {{ill|1957|Q5311|qid=Q5311}} (1957) {{ill|Kinnosuke Kamino|Q26485958|qid=Q26485958|lt=Kinnosuke Kamino}} and relocated it to its current location.
* Tea room "Seisetsuan" - A tea room located in the residence of Shinichi Ito, a tinsel merchant. {{ill|1948|Q5165|qid=Q5165}} It was moved to its current location in June 1948.
* Tea room "Rokuyuken" - Built by the Rokuyukai, a group of art dealers, and named by {{ill|Masuda Takashi|Q786186|qid=Q786186|lt=Nuno Masuda}}. In {{ill|1947|Q5263|qid=Q5263}} (Showa 22), it was dedicated by the Rokuyukai on the occasion of the establishment of the Atsuta Jingu Kencha Association, and was moved to its current location.
* Tea room "Hoan" - A Sukiya style tea room dedicated by Hikojiro Takahashi. {{ill|1966|Q2649|qid=Q2649}}Completed on October 1, 1966.
* Tea room "Homukentei" - Formerly a tea room. The name Hoken is derived from the haiku name Hoan, written by Hikojiro Takahashi, who renovated this tea ceremony room, and from Toyohiko Inui's ``inui.'' {{ill|1977|Q2481|qid=Q2481}} (1977) Restoration.* {{ill|Ryōeikaku|Q11679252|qid=Q11679252}} (National Registered Tangible Cultural Property) - Former Nagoya Museum Exhibition Center. Built in {{ill|1878|Q7776|qid=Q7776}} (Meiji 11), moved to Shonai Park in {{ill|1932|Q18743|qid=Q18743}} (Showa 7), and moved to its current location in {{ill|1968|Q2644|qid=Q2644}} (Showa 43).
* Minamo Temple
* Garden "Magatama-en" - A pond with a curved ball pond {{ill|Strolling garden|Q11420231|qid=Q11420231}}.
* {{ill|Atsuta Jingū Museum|Q11569116|qid=Q11569116|lt=Treasure Hall}} (Culture Hall) - It has approximately 6,000 items donated by {{ill|National Treasure (Japan)|Q1139795|qid=Q1139795}}, {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Q1188622|qid=Q1188622}}, {{ill|Imperial House of Japan|Q909452|qid=Q909452}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tokugawa Shogun Family}}, {{ill|Owari Tokugawa family|Q841740|qid=Q841740}}, etc.
* Treasure Hall Annex
* Sakuma Toro - When the fourth son {{ill|Sakuma Katsuyuki|Q10885889|qid=Q10885889|lt=Katsuyuki}} of Gokidokoro Castle Lord {{ill|Sakuma Moritsugu|Q10885892|qid=Q10885892}} encountered a typhoon at sea, he visited Atsuta Shrine. When he prayed to the shrine for protection, he escaped the disaster, so he donated it as a thank you in {{ill|Kan'ei|Q1192913|qid=Q1192913}}7 ({{ill|1630|Q6856|qid=Q6856}}). <ref>From the local information board</ref> Known as one of Japan's three major lanterns.

=== Betsugu/Setsusha ===
{{Anchors|Bekku|Setsusha}}Within the main shrine, there are 1 annex shrine, 8 setsushas, and 19 subsidiary shrines within the precincts, and 4 setshas and 12 subsidiary shrines outside the precincts, making a total of 45 shrines (including the main shrine). |group="Note"}}<ref>[http://www.atsutajingu.or.jp/jingu/about/yukari/ Bekku, Setsusha, Suesha] (Atsuta Jingu official website). </ref>.

===Buildings of the past===
There used to be three gates connected to the Nobunaga wall, the Kaizomon (Kaizomon), which was designated as a national treasure in {{ill|1920|Q2155|qid=Q2155}} (Taisho 9), and the Chinkomon and Shunshomon, which are also national treasures, but they were destroyed by fire during the Nagoya Air Raid during the Pacific War. After the war, the cultural properties of Atsuta Shrine that had been lost in the war were not rebuilt or restored. In {{ill|2022|Q49625|qid=Q49625}} (Reiwa 4), Atsuta City's history experience project <ref>[https://www.city.nagoya.jp/atsuta/page/0000155998.html Atsuta City's history experience project "Atsuta History Exploration" has begun! (PDF: 6306KB) - As part of the {{ill|Augmented reality|Q254183|qid=Q254183}} project as part of Nagoya City]</ref>, the Sea Gate was commissioned and supervised by architect {{ill|Masayuki Miura|Q11356475|qid=Q11356475}}{{ill|Hiroshima University|Q115220|qid=Q115220}}. A reconstruction map of the Maritime Gate was created based on materials such as traces of the foundation stone of the Upper Gate, and the Maritime Gate was reproduced with 3DCG <ref>[https://www.city.nagoya.jp/atsuta/cmsfiles/contents/0000155/155998/panelAR.pdf Restoration of Atsuta Jingu Maritime Gate, a former national treasure (PDF: 6306KB) - Nagoya City]</ref>.

Postcard of Gate Kaijo-Mon Atsuta Shrine Scan10007.jpg|Picture postcard of the former national treasure building, Maritime Gate (Kaizomon, no longer extant)
</gallery>
}}

=== Cultural assets ===
Because the Kusanagi sword is a sacred object, many swords have been donated to Atsuta Shrine from the local community, and the shrine has approximately 450 swords in its collection. More than 30 of them are designated cultural properties by the country and prefecture. October 4, 2021</ref>.

* Amida Sutra Volume 1 - Kamakura period, decorative paper ink calligraphy.
* Heart Sutra Volume 1 - 3rd year of the Karei era, ink and paper.
* Letter from Sanmihoin Jozeki (Yoshifusa Miyoshi) 1 page - Edo period, ink and paper on paper.
* Horaku Kasen Renga Kaishi, 1 volume - Muromachi period, 1996, sketch on writing paper.* 312 chapters of Atsuta Manku of 13th and 4th Kan'ei years - Edo period, historical material on haiku literature, 1. Atsuta Manku of 13th Kanei period, 2. Added Atsuta Manku of 13th Kanei period, 3. Manku of Atsuta of 14th year of Kanei era (Class A), 4. Manku of Atsuta of 14th year of Kanei era (Class B).
* Atsuta Shrine Baba Family Documents Volume 8 - Jingu worship materials from the Kamakura period to the Edo period.
* 1 piece of iron gilt-copper-clad horse harness - Kofun period, dedicated in 1993, excavated from Shiratori Tumulus, archaeological material.

=== Notes ===
* In {{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}} established in the late {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, Ichinomiya in Owari Province was {{ill|Masumida Shrine|Q705916|qid=Q705916}} and Atsuta Shrine was considered Sannomiya. There are various theories regarding this, and {{ill|Hiroshi Inoue|Q11372970|qid=Q11372970}} states that Atsuta Shrine was initially treated as a special shrine.{{Efn2|In the June 1st year of Eiman era, the Order of the Shrines of the Jingikan (Heian Ibun No. 3358), it was written as ``Owari Province Ichinomiya Ninomiya Atsuta Shrine,'' and Atsuta Shrine was not considered to be a Sannomiya Shrine. }} and the active efforts of Masumita Shrine <ref>Kanji Inoue, "Japan's Medieval State and the Ichinomiya System of the Provinces," Iwata Shoin, 2009, pp. 95–98. </ref>The theory is that {{ill|Susumu Uejima|Q24576799|qid=Q24576799}} initially had the status of Ichinomiya, but later the conflict between the Kokuga and Atsuta Shrine influenced the change of Ichinomiya. </ref> is issued. In any case, at the end of the Heian period (late 12th century), when the order of domestic shrines centered on Ichinomiya was established, Atsuta Jingu came to be positioned as Sannomiya, and Atsuta Jingu avoided calling itself Sannomiya by using expressions such as ``Chinju Sansha'' <ref>Owari Kokushicho Sendan (Kamakura Ibun No. 3401) dated 1st year of Karoku</ref>.*{{ill|Saigyō|Q224689|qid=Q224689}} "Nijyugocho Bridge", where legend has it that a monk sat down to rest.{{Efn2|It consists of 25 stone slabs. }} appears in {{ill|Owari meisho zue|Q11465290|qid=Q11465290}} and Nagoya Jinku, and is said to be the oldest stone bridge in Nagoya.
* In the {{ill|Japan Collegiate Ekiden Championships|Q11390082|qid=Q11390082}} to be held in November, Nishimon Torii-mae ({{ill|Japan National Route 19|Q899326|qid=Q899326}}) will be used as the starting point.
* At the {{ill|1936 Summer Olympics|Q8150|qid=Q8150|lt=Berlin Olympics}} in {{ill|1936|Q18649|qid=Q18649}}, female swimmer {{ill|Hideko Maehata|Q271612|qid=Q271612}} swallowed several Atsuta Shrine charms and placed them in her stomach just before the race, winning the gold medal.
* Ryukagekaku, built as a resting place for {{ill|Emperor Meiji|Q174231|qid=Q174231}}, is registered as a national {{ill|Registered Tangible Cultural Property of Japan|Q11579194|qid=Q11579194}}. From the north window, you can see the Nobunaga Wall, one of Japan's three major earthen walls, dedicated to {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|Q171411|qid=Q171411}}, and from the south window, you can see Magatama Pond and the garden, which is colored with seasonal flowers.
* The pond inside Magatama-en that is modeled after {{ill|Magatama|Q334232|qid=Q334232}}, one of the {{ill|Imperial Regalia of Japan|Q327465|qid=Q327465}}, is called Magatama (Magatama) Pond. One of the bridges that spans there is a bridge called ``Akahashi'', and it is said that two people who swear their love on this bridge will be happy, so the locals call it ``Fukuyosebashi'', a bridge that brings good fortune.

=== Atsuta Okage Yokocho Plan ===Atsuta Shrine used to have a thriving temple town, so there are plans to recreate a bustling temple town like Ise's {{ill|Okage Yokochō|Q11261371|qid=Q11261371}} near Atsuta Shrine.{{ill|2011|Q1994|qid=Q1994}}<ref>[http://www.nup.or.jp/nui/user/media/document/investigation/h22/shimin1.pdf Atsuta Shrine's gate street. ．． ．． - Nagoya Town Development Corporation top page]</ref>. The maintenance plan itself was {{ill|Jingū-mae Station|Q6202481|qid=Q6202481|lt=Meitetsu Jingumae Station}} of Atsuta Jingu Shrine, which Nagoya City called "Atsuta Sando City" in {{ill|1988|Q2426|qid=Q2426}}. There was a redevelopment plan to improve the area including the shopping street, but due to various circumstances the plan failed and was set back <ref>[https://milepost.exblog.jp/28548730/ What was the redevelopment plan for the Atsuta Jingu Station area 30 years ago?: Record of town development activities (Nagoya Gakuin University Mizuno)]</ref>. {{ill|Takashi Kawamura (politician)|Q440000|qid=Q440000}} Former Nagoya mayor also pledged to improve ``Atsuta Kusanagi Yokocho'' during the April mayoral election. {{ill|2018|Q25291|qid=Q25291}}Atsuta-Jingu Station Area Town Development Council was launched in April <ref>[https://www.city.nagoya.jp/jutakutoshi/cmsfiles/contents/0000057/57993/atsutakousou.pdf Atsuta-Jingu Station Area Town Development Plan]</ref>. {{ill|2024|Q49619|qid=Q49619}} In July, Nagoya City once again presented a redevelopment plan for Jingumae Station. Nihon Keizai Shimbun]</ref>. On {{ill|September 6|Q2858|qid=Q2858}} in 2024, {{ill|Atsuta nagAya|Q130240709|qid=Q130240709}} by {{ill|Meitetsu|Q30850|qid=Q30850}}, which is different from the Nagoya City plan mentioned above, began operations west of Meitetsu Jingumae Station.

=== Tradition ===
*The Atsuta area of Atsuta Shrine has been known as ``{{ill|Mount Penglai|Q798391|qid=Q798391|lt=Horaijima}}'' since ancient times, and was even written about in books from the Kamakura period. Since ancient times, {{pronounced kana|Noshio Ichigata|Ayuchigata}}{{Efn2|{{pronounced kana|Nengoichigata|Ayuchigata}} is {{jalink|Aichi County} which appeared at the end of the {{ill|Ice age|Q49367|qid=Q49367|lt=Ice Age}} due to a sea level rise called {{ill|Holocene glacial retreat|Q834405|qid=Q834405}}. (Aichi Prefecture)|Q552687|Formerly Aichi District}} refers to the {{ill|Mudflat|Q31796|qid=Q31796}} that spread throughout the area. }}, Atsuta Shrine, which is overgrown with old pine cedar trees over 1,000 years old, looks like a cape jutting out into the sea, and was likened to being on the shell of a giant turtle.Therefore, Atsuta Shrine was referred to as Horai Island (in books introducing Japan), the home of the immortal {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shins}}. It is said that this is because it was imitated by a Chinese legend from the Tang Dynasty. Atsuta ``The Legend of Hourai'']</ref>.*Atsuta Shrine has a legend related to {{ill|Yang Guifei|Q298046|qid=Q298046}}. ambitious {{ill|Emperor Xuanzong of Tang|Q9746|qid=Q9746|lt=Emperor Xuanzong}} was waiting for an opportunity to invade Japan. The Japanese gods who knew about this quickly got together and discussed how to deal with it, and as a result, Atsuta Daimyojin transformed into an assassin and an unparalleled beauty, approached Genso, and used her beauty to seduce Genso so that he would not invade Japan. Although his first mission was successful, his true identity was revealed and he was later killed. The spirit of Atsuta Daimyojin, which had transformed into Yang Guifei, returned to Atsuta. Based on the legend of Yang Guifei, a tomb for Yang Guifei was built at Shimizu Shrine, but it was demolished during the renovation of Atsuta Shrine in the early Meiji period. {{Citation required|date=August 2025}}

* {{ill|Omiya Shrine (Iwade City)|Q11434451|qid=Q11434451}} ({{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|Q131314|qid=Q131314}}{{ill|Iwade, Wakayama|Q579623|qid=Q579623}}) - It is said that during the reign of Emperor Genmei (712), Nihon Takeru was solicited from Atsuta Shrine in Owari and it became a village shrine.* {{ill|Owari-to Shrine|ja|尾張戸神社|qid=Q11465305}} (Aichi Prefecture Nagoya City {{ill|Moriyama-ku, Nagoya|Q1155291|qid=Q1155291}}, {{ill|Seto, Aichi|ar|سيتو (آيتشي)|azb|ستو، آیچی|ca|Seto|ce|Сето (Айти)|ceb|Seto (lungsod)|ckb|سێتۆ، ئایچی|cs|Seto|de|Seto (Aichi)|eo|Seto (Ajĉio)|es|Seto (Aichi)|fa|ستو، آیچی|fi|Seto (Aichi)|fr|Seto|gl|Seto|hy|Սետո|id|Seto, Aichi|it|Seto|ja|瀬戸市|ko|세토시|lt|Setas (Aičis)|mg|Seto|mzn|ستو، آیچی|nl|Seto (Aichi)|no|Seto|pl|Seto (miasto)|pnb|سیٹو|pt|Seto|ro|Seto|ru|Сето (Айти)|sh|Seto|sr|Сето|sv|Seto|tg|Сето|tl|Seto, Aichi|tr|Seto|tt|Сето (Айти)|uk|Сето (Айті)|ur|سیتو، ایچی|uz|Seto (Aichi)|vi|Seto, Aichi|war|Seto, Aichi|zh|瀨戶市|zh_classical|瀨戶市|zh_min_nan|Seto-chhī|zh_yue|瀨戶|qid=Q499493}}) - This shrine is said to have been built in 5th year of the 13th Emperor, {{ill|Emperor Seimu|Q316672|qid=Q316672}}, at the request of Miyazakihime, to enshrine the founder of the Owari clan.It is a shrine located on the summit of {{ill|Mount Togoku|ja|東谷山|lld|Mont Tōgoku|qid=Q11528351}}, the sacred mountain of the Owari clan, and is also known as ``Atsuta no Okunoin.''
* {{ill|Fujidango|Q11404985|qid=Q11404985|lt=Fujidango}} (Judango) - A famous sweet sold around Atsuta Shrine.
* {{ill|Kaminoi Shuzo|ja|神の井酒造|qid=Q22125473}} - A sake brewing company named after the third generation head of the family donated the Saita of Atsuta Shrine.
* {{ill|Senshū Suetaka|Q48760362|qid=Q48760362}} - A member of the House of Peers' Baron from the Daiguji Chiaki clan.
